top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, experimentally demonstrated new measurement capability: the magic-wavelength condition is a genuine physical idea, 10^-18 uncertainty has been reproduced by independent laboratories, and the instrument has already delivered millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and many-body physics inside the clock. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scope (invention and realization, no redefinition of the second) is defensible. Twisted bilayer graphene is a strong, field-opening discovery but the three-name credit and citation scope are less settled, so it ranks second; no award is worse than either mature option.
